subject: SOC 2 coverage + EU hosting — data export & bridge letter playbook
messages:
From: Elena Mäkinen <elena.makinen@finserve.eu>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-03T09:15:00Z
Subject: SOC2 request and hosting / data export questions

Hi Rishi,

We're kicking off procurement for a production rollout and have a few compliance items we need to resolve before we can proceed. Could you please provide: 

- The latest SOC 2 Type II report (audit period and tested controls).
- A draft bridge letter (or confirmation you can supply one) that covers the gap between the report's end date and the contract start.
- Clarification on hosting region options for the Hosted API — specifically whether customer data for EU tenants is processed and retained inside the EU for hosted customers.
- An explicit statement about cross-border transfers: do any subprocessors or telemetry pipelines route customer content to the US or other non-EU locations? If so, what controls/SCCs are in place?
- Details on encryption & key management options (BYOK, KMS, key residency).
- A list of subprocessors relevant to hosting and logging.

We'd like to have the SOC2 report and a provisional bridge letter by next week if possible so procurement can move forward.

Thanks,
Elena
Procurement Manager | FinServe EU

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Elena Mäkinen <elena.makinen@finserve.eu>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-03T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC2 request and hosting / data export questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I can get the SOC 2 Type II report and a bridge letter template over to you. Looping in Laura from Legal and Grace from Security to provide the specifics on hosting region, subprocessors, and KMS options.

Quick clarifying Q: can you confirm whether you need an attestation that "no customer content will leave the EU" for hosted EU customers, or whether contractual protections/SCCs and technical controls are sufficient? That will help us scope the language in the bridge.

I can send the preliminary docs by EOD Friday (our side) — legal/security will follow with technical language.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Enterprise | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0192

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Mäkinen <elena.makinen@finserve.eu>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-04T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC2 request and hosting / data export questions

Hi Elena — Laura here (Legal). Thanks for the note and the timeline. Please find attached the SOC 2 Type II report for the most recent audit ("SOC2_Redwood_TypeII_2025.pdf") which covers the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31 and the controls tested during that window.

On the bridge letter: we can provide a signed bridge letter that: 
- Confirms there have been no material scope changes or exceptions since the last report date, and
- Affirms the operating effectiveness of the same controls during the interim period (we provide the signed template as a starting point).

We have attached a draft bridge template (SOC2_bridge_template_2026-05.docx). If you want specific language about data residency for hosted EU tenants we can add a tailored paragraph; please note the distinction below: 

Hosting / data residency options — high level (for procurement):
- Hosted (public) EU region: primary processing and storage for an EU tenant configured in our EU region (eu-west-1) occurs in-region. We can provide an architecture diagram on request.
- Dedicated / Private: customers can deploy in a VPC or on-prem where no cross-border transfer occurs unless explicitly enabled. Dedicated customers can also elect Azure/AWS region options under contract.

Cross-border transfer & legal safeguards:
- For Hosted EU region tenants, operational telemetry (aggregated logs, billing metadata) is processed by services that may have components in multiple regions for operational purposes. We apply strict minimization and encryption controls.
- We execute a DPA that includes Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for transfers outside the EEA and offer Model Clauses / Binding Corporate Rules where applicable. See attached DPA_Redwood_2024.pdf.

Subprocessors relevant to hosting and logging are listed in our subprocessor registry; the primary ones are: cloud provider (AWS eu-west-1), CDN provider, and monitoring/telemetry partner (analytics). We can provide a scoped list for procurement.

If you require a hard "no export" statement for the Hosted offering (i.e., absolute guarantee that data will never leave the EU under all configurations), that's only possible for Private/Dedicated deployments with contractual and technical controls (BYOK + no external telemetry routing). We can outline an approach to get close to that guarantee for Hosted customers, but it will have caveats regarding aggregated telemetry and third-party operational access.

Next steps: 
- Grace will follow up on encryption/KMS and technical controls.
- Neha (Legal) is available to review bridge language for procurement.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment(s): SOC2_Redwood_TypeII_2025.pdf; SOC2_bridge_template_2026-05.docx; DPA_Redwood_2024.pdf

From: Elena Mäkinen <elena.makinen@finserve.eu>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finserve.eu
Date: 2026-05-04T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC2 request and hosting / data export questions

Thanks Laura — useful detail. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) For procurement we need either (A) an explicit contractual attestation that customer content for EU-hosted tenants will not be transferred outside the EU, or (B) a clear list of exceptions with SCCs and a description of telemetry minimization. Which of those is feasible for Hosted customers?

2) For encryption: can you confirm whether Hosted EU tenants can use KMS keys provisioned in an EU region (customer-managed KMS), or is BYOK limited to Dedicated/Private only?

3) Subprocessor list: please provide the scoped list for hosting + logging as soon as possible.

If (A) is not possible for Hosted, we will need explicit language in the bridge and the DPA describing exactly what telemetry/metadata may be processed outside the EU and what safeguards are in place.

Regards,
Elena

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Elena Mäkinen <elena.makinen@finserve.eu>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-05T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC2 request and hosting / data export questions

Hi Elena — Grace from Security here. Quick answers and options below.

Encryption & Key Management:
- Hosted (EU region): we support TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. For hosted EU tenants we can provision customer-specific KMS keys that are region-scoped (EU) for at-rest encryption of storage volumes and object stores. This is currently provided as a managed KMS option (Redwood-managed keys with EU residency).
- BYOK (customer-supplied keys): BYOK is available for Dedicated and Private deployments today. For the hosted multi-tenant public offering, BYOK is not generally available due to the operational model; we can discuss a scoped solution for larger enterprise commitments.

Telemetry & cross-border processing:
- Primary content processing for an EU-configured tenant is performed within eu-west-1.
- Aggregated telemetry (metrics, anonymized traces used for runtime optimization) may be routed through control plane services which currently have components outside the EU for operational reliability. These telemetry streams do not include plaintext customer content.
- Controls in place: encryption in transit, data minimization, access controls, and SCCs in the DPA for any transfers. We also retain audit logs that show access to keys and administrative actions.

Subprocessor list (scoped to hosting & logging):
- AWS (eu-west-1) — compute & object storage
- FastCDN Ltd. — global CDN (edge caching only; config can be restricted to EU where required)
- Loglytics Inc. — metrics/monitoring (ingests aggregated/obfuscated telemetry)

If you need an explicit statement for procurement that "no customer content will leave the EU for EU-hosted tenants," we can provide a narrow attestation that applies to primary processing and storage, but must add the following caveat in the same sentence: "excluding aggregated operational telemetry and metadata required for platform health, which may be processed outside the EU under SCCs and with technical minimization." Alternatively, Dedicated/Private with BYOK is the path to an auditable, contractually enforceable no-export posture.

Deliverables we can produce this week:
- Signed bridge letter (customized paragraph about hosting residency per your preference)
- Scoped subprocessor list for hosting & logging (CSV)
- KMS options summary (attached)

Let me know which wording you prefer in the bridge and I will have Legal bake it into the template.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Attachment(s): KMS_options_summary.pdf

From: Elena Mäkinen <elena.makinen@finserve.eu>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finserve.eu
Date: 2026-05-06T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC2 request and hosting / data export questions

Hi Grace / Laura / Rishi — thanks for the detailed responses and the attachments. Procurement would prefer the bridge to include the tailored paragraph you suggested that: 

"Primary processing and storage of customer content for tenants configured in the EU-hosted region (eu-west-1) will remain within the EU. Aggregated operational telemetry and minimal metadata required for platform operations may be processed outside the EU under Redwood's DPA and SCCs; such telemetry does not contain customer plaintext content and is subject to encryption and access controls."

Please prepare that paragraph in the signed bridge letter. Also please attach the scoped subprocessor list (hosting + logging) and the short KMS options summary for our security checklist. Once we have the signed bridge and the CSV, procurement will finalize the PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena
Procurement Manager | FinServe EU
